main_risks: Implementation is not a small filter patch; generic CUDA MMVQ assumes Q8_1 activation layout.
The 10 tok/s overhead budget is only about 1.64s if all decode up/down fallback is removed, so a naive kernel will not be enough.
Any added VRAM workspace must not steal the accepted 13.2GiB gate cache or break the 16GB host cgroup including page cache.
minimum_design: Extend CPU call site to pass params->wdata Q8_0 rows and row_size_stream to ggml_cuda_moe_stream_one when an explicit diagnostic env is set.
Add a specialized CUDA MXFP4 x Q8_0 MMVQ/rows helper instead of using the existing Q8_1 helper.
Keep the accepted gate-only SOTA path unchanged by default.
First run llama-results top1 verifier; only if 145/145 passes, run strict cold token-rate benchmark.
candidate.name: default-off MXFP4 x Q8_0 CUDA one-stream path for up/down
candidate.screening_decision: worth designing as the next exact compute/offload candidate; do not implement as a blind full benchmark
candidate.why_possible: It would use the same Q8_0 activation quantization semantics as CPU fallback, removing the Q8_1 drift that can flip low-margin top1 positions, while targeting the only remaining bottleneck class with a 10 tok/s no-overhead ceiling.

source_facts.fact: CPU MXFP4 fallback uses ggml_vec_dot_mxfp4_q8_0 and vec_dot_type GGML_TYPE_Q8_0
CUDA MMVQ MXFP4 path uses quantize_row_q8_1_cuda and vec_dot_mxfp4_q8_1
